turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry we rolled in late, she fought the car seat the whole way. This is Maya, she just turned four.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're fine. Have a seat. What brought you in?
[SEG0003] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's her ear. She cried on and off all night and kept grabbing the right side. We just came through a cold.
[SEG0004] person_3 (PATIENT): Ear hurt.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Aw, Maya. Can you point to the one that hurts?
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): Right. No touch.
[SEG0007] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Right ear, yeah. She swats my hand away. She's tired and just plain irritable today.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): How many nights has she been up with it?
[SEG0009] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Um. Two? Well, actually three. Sunday was the first really bad night, so three nights.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the cold, when did that start?
[SEG0011] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Runny nose and a cough, about a week ago, give or take. Nose is mostly done. There's still a little cough, mostly when she lies down, nothing dramatic.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Has she had a fever with this?
[SEG0013] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. I checked a couple of times at home and it was normal, like 98 something.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Did anybody else think she felt warm?
[SEG0015] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): My mom did. She had Maya yesterday and texted that she felt hot. No thermometer, though. I wasn't there, so I can't really say.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright. I'll hold both of those, your readings were normal, and Grandma thought she felt hot without a number. Any pus or blood from the ear?
[SEG0017] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Nothing leaking.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about throwing up, or loose stools?
[SEG0019] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She threw up once, no, wait, that was the stomach bug last month. Not with this. She's eating less, picky, but she's drinking milk and juice okay.
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Juice.
[SEG0021] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): When we're done, promise. Ugh, I think the parking meter's gonna run out. Not important.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is she tugging the ear in the daytime too, or is it mainly nights?
[SEG0023] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Nights are awful, like screaming awful. Daytime she tugs if she's worn out. Daycare said she was fussy yesterday but she did play a little.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anybody else at home or daycare sick?
[SEG0025] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Half her class had colds. Her brother, he's six, had the same cold and he's over it. He's the one with asthma. He takes montelukast. Maya does not.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Montelukast stays his, not hers. What is Maya actually taking right now?

[SEG0027] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Children's ibuprofen, the liquid, by mouth. It's a hundred milligrams in five mils, and I give five mils, not a teaspoon like I almost said. Every six hours or so when she hurts, and the last one was around six, maybe seven, this morning.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): So 100 milligrams by mouth, roughly every six hours as needed for the ear pain. Any antibiotic or ear drops recently?
[SEG0029] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Urgent care, two weeks ago, handed us ofloxacin drops. They thought swimmer's ear. I never opened them. She never got a drop.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then they don't count. Has she been on anything you stopped?

[SEG0031] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Cetirizine, five milligrams at night, by mouth. Her pediatrician started it last fall for the endless sniffles, and I stopped it in March once that calmed down. Nothing since.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any medicine allergies?

[SEG0033] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I don't think so. Well, actually, long ago, I couldn't tell you when, maybe when she was one, they gave her amoxicillin. I think she got a rash, or it was just the virus. My husband says rash, I'm fuzzy, we never gave it again, and I'm not sure it's a real allergy.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Possible amoxicillin rash, not certain, and the timing's unclear. We will not use amoxicillin. Foods or anything else?

[SEG0035] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, nothing else I know of. Oh, side note, my husband takes metformin for his diabetes. And my sister is always pushing her biotin gummies. Neither of those is for Maya, I didn't give them.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Those aren't hers, and I won't list them. Maya, I need to peek in the ears. I'll be quick.
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): No!
[SEG0038] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I know, baby. Mama's right here. She slept maybe four hours, tops, so she's fried.

[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right drum is red and a little bulging. Left drum looks normal. Throat's mildly pink, and there's a bit of clear mucus in the nose. Neck is soft without worrisome nodes, and the lungs are clear.
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): All done?
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Just about. Here she's 98.4, heart rate 112, oxygen 99 percent, breathing easy at 22.
[SEG0042] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So no fever in the office either.

[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Correct, not right now. Putting this together, it looks like an early ear infection on the right after that cold. She's drinking, and I don't have a measured fever, so it isn't a severe one.
[SEG0044] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Are we starting antibiotics? She was screaming last night.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not today. This is a reasonable spot for watchful waiting. Keep the ibuprofen, same 100 milligrams by mouth every six hours or so, with a snack if her tummy's off.
[SEG0046] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We've got children's acetaminophen at home. I haven't given her any this week. I was scared of doubling up.

[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): You may alternate acetaminophen if the pain breaks through between ibuprofen doses. Don't give them at the same time. I'm not putting her on it as a standing medicine unless you need that.
[SEG0048] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Okay. And if tonight is another disaster?

[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Backup plan. I'll send cefdinir suspension, 125 milligrams by mouth twice a day for five days. Only start it if she is still miserable, or if she gets a real fever, after two days. Not tonight.
[SEG0050] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Cefdinir. If that maybe-rash was actually an allergy, is this safe?

[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's a different drug family enough that, with only a possible rash years ago, it's a fair backup. Hives, swelling, or trouble breathing, you stop and get help. If she just perks up, you don't start it.
[SEG0052] person_3 (PATIENT): Go home.
[SEG0053] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Soon, hon. She lives with me and her dad, by the way, if you need that. Daycare tomorrow, yes or no?

[SEG0054] person_2 (DOCTOR): Keep her home tomorrow while she's this uncomfortable. She can go back once the pain has settled and she's herself, even if you never start the cefdinir. No swimming till the ear's quiet.
[SEG0055] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And leave the cetirizine stopped? Those ofloxacin drops just sit in the cabinet.

[SEG0056] person_2 (DOCTOR): Leave cetirizine off, it isn't for an ear infection. Don't use the old drops, they were for something else and she never started them. If you come back unsure, bring the bottle.

[SEG0057] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): If she's not better in two days I start the cefdinir and I bring her back, right? Grandma's gonna say I should've demanded a shot. I'll just tell her what you said.

[SEG0058] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes. If she's not clearly better in two days, start the cefdinir and come back. Sooner if she won't drink, seems worse, or you measure a fever over 102. You handled a cranky morning well, and we're done for today.

spec.situation: Mother and a child with ear pain and night crying after a cold; mother says no fever, grandmother says it was hot; mother unsure about the amoxicillin the child had 'long ago, got a rash maybe'; doctor decides on watchful waiting with a back-up plan.
features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

bad.reason: Diabetes is supported, but relation is husband/father of family member, not explicitly Maya's father.
Amoxicillin was previously given, but not described as a discontinued current medication.
Help/sooner return precautions supported; transcript says stop 'it' after reaction, not specifically cefdinir.

Recent medication history missing: urgent care prescribed ofloxacin ear drops two weeks ago for presumed swimmer's ear, but the bottle was never opened and she never received any drops.

The record wrongly lists amoxicillin as a discontinued medication; in the transcript it was only a remote prior exposure with a possible rash and uncertain allergy, not a current or recently discontinued medicine.
History detail missing: she slept maybe four hours total the previous night.
Plan threshold detail missing: cefdinir should be started only if she is still miserable or gets a real fever after two days, specifically 'not tonight.'
Return precaution detail missing: come back and start cefdinir if she is not clearly better in two days.

omissions.text: Runny nose is mostly resolved but not completely gone; there is still a little clear nasal mucus.
The child had no measured fever at home, with temperatures '98-something,' and no fever in clinic; the report that she 'felt hot' came only from grandmother without a thermometer.
Family member specifically said Maya is not taking montelukast; the montelukast belongs to her brother with asthma.
Last ibuprofen dose was around 6 to 7 AM the morning of the visit.
Ofloxacin ear drops from urgent care two weeks earlier were prescribed for presumed swimmer's ear, but they were never opened and Maya never received any drops.

The possible amoxicillin reaction details are more uncertain than recorded: family member was unsure whether there was any rash at all versus a viral rash, timing was unclear, and they have avoided amoxicillin since.
Neck exam was described as soft without worrisome nodes, not just absence of cervical lymphadenopathy.
Respiratory exam included 'breathing easy' in addition to RR 22 and clear lungs.
Use acetaminophen only if pain breaks through between ibuprofen doses, and do not give acetaminophen and ibuprofen at the same time.
Do not start cefdinir tonight; only start after two days if still miserable or if she develops a real fever.
